title: Reporting with passives; It is said that ...
subtitle: It is reported that ... / The damage is reported to be ...
summary: Report what an unnamed group of people say or think using passives: it is said that ..., the damage is reported to be ..., and there are thought to be ...

lesson.heading: Reporting with a passive
lesson.text: We often use a passive to report what people say, think, decide and so on, particularly when it is not important to mention **who** is being reported.

examples.text: People in the area **have been told** that they should stay indoors.
Everyone **was asked** to bring some food to the party.

lesson.heading: it + passive verb + that-clause
lesson.text: Another common way of reporting what an unspecified group of people say is **it + passive verb + that-clause**. It lets us keep the important information until the end of the sentence.

examples.text: **It is reported that** the damage is extensive.
examples.note: compare The damage is extensive, according to government sources.

examples.text: **It was decided that** the meeting should be cancelled.
examples.note: or It was decided to cancel the meeting.

lesson.note: Also: allege, announce, assume, believe, calculate, claim, consider, demonstrate, discover, establish, estimate, expect, feel, find, know, mention, recommend, reveal, say, show, suggest, suppose, think, understand; agree, decide, hope, intend, plan, propose (these last six can also be followed by a to-infinitive clause).

lesson.heading: Verbs that need a personal object
lesson.text: Many other reporting verbs are **not** used in the it + passive + that-clause pattern, because in the active they need a personal object before the that-clause (*They have informed us that ...*). They can still be used as in section A.

examples.text: We **have been informed that** we have to leave.
examples.note: not It has been informed that we have to leave

lesson.note: Also: encourage, persuade, reassure, remind, tell, warn.

lesson.heading: subject + passive verb + to-infinitive
lesson.text: An alternative is to make the person or thing the **subject**, if we want it to be the topic of the sentence. Most of the verbs above work here, except *announce, decide, mention, propose, recommend* and *suggest*.

examples.text: It is reported that the damage is extensive. - **The damage is reported to be** extensive.
I **was told** (= ordered) **to go** with them to the railway station.
examples.note: tell works here only when it means 'order'

examples.text: It was said that the accident had happened just after midnight.
examples.wrong: The accident was told to have happened just after midnight

lesson.heading: it + passive verb + wh-clause
lesson.text: With some verbs we can also report information that has been given or found out with **it + passive verb + a wh-clause**.

examples.text: **It has now been revealed who** was responsible for the accident.
The decision to build the bridge was taken before **it was established whether** it was actually needed.

lesson.note: Also: discover, explain, find, know, reveal, show, understand.

lesson.heading: there + passive verb + to be
lesson.text: When the that-clause begins **that + there ...**, we can make a matching passive with **there + passive verb + to be / to have been**.

examples.text: It is thought (that) there are too many obstacles to peace.
**There are thought to be** too many obstacles to peace.

lesson.note: The same verbs work here as in the subject + passive verb + to-infinitive pattern.

lesson.text: Choose it is said that ... when the news is the point, and the King is said to be ... when the person or thing is already the topic.

exercises.prompt: TERRORISTS BELIEVED TO BE OPERATING IN BERLIN - ___ that terrorists are operating in Berlin.
exercises.explanation: it + passive verb + that-clause reports what an unnamed group believes.

exercises.prompt: WATER DISCOVERED ON MARS - ___ that there is water on Mars.
exercises.explanation: A recent discovery takes the present perfect passive: it has been discovered that ...

exercises.prompt: It was ___ to hold new negotiations next month.
exercises.explanation: agree can be followed by a to-infinitive clause in this pattern; announce cannot, and reassure needs a personal object.

exercises.prompt: Which verbs can be used in the pattern It is / has been ... that ...?
categories: No: the verb needs a personal object

exercises.prompt: Rewrite the headline AGREEMENT THAT UN WILL SEND IN TROOPS as a passive sentence with it.
exercises.answer: It has been agreed that the UN will send in troops
exercises.explanation: it + passive verb + that-clause keeps the news until the end.

exercises.prompt: Which headline cannot be rewritten as a passive sentence beginning with It ... that ... ?
options: MOON ASTRONAUTS EXPECTED TO RETURN TODAY
exercises.explanation: reassure needs a personal object, so we say Patients have been reassured that ..., not It has been reassured that ...

exercises.prompt: It has not yet been ___ who was responsible for the error.
exercises.explanation: Only some verbs take a wh-clause in this pattern: explain does, claim does not.

exercises.prompt: We don't think that the fault is serious. - The fault ___ to be serious.
exercises.explanation: subject + passive verb + to-infinitive puts the fault first as the topic.

exercises.prompt: We expect that it will take several weeks to correct the fault. - The fault ___ to take several weeks to correct.
exercises.explanation: expect works in both patterns: It is expected that ... and The fault is expected to ...

exercises.statement: It has been decided to postpone the next rocket launch.
exercises.explanation: Correct. decide is one of the verbs that can be followed by a to-infinitive clause after it + passive verb.

exercises.prompt: It is thought that there are too many obstacles to peace. - There ___ too many obstacles to peace.
exercises.explanation: A that + there ... clause becomes there + passive verb + to be.

exercises.statement: The next launch is suggested to take place in May.
exercises.explanation: It is suggested that the next launch should take place in May. suggest is not used in the subject + passive verb + to-infinitive pattern.
